subject: PrivateNet launch criteria & ownership decision
messages:
From: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.ai>
To: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>, Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Andrew Bailey <andrew@acmeanalytics.com>
Date: 2028-03-02T09:12:00Z
Subject: PrivateNet launch criteria & ownership decision

Team —

Acme has asked us to define a path to run Redwood in their private VPC and a co-located on-prem site (they call it "PrivateNet"). Before we lock the pilot scope I need clarity on: ownership, acceptance criteria, and the minimum resourcing required from Infra/Platform/Product/Sec/Legal.

Can each of you confirm the following by EOD today or in tomorrow's sync: 
- Owner for architecture decisions (who signs off on infra topology)
- Security gating checklist owner (SOC2 evidence, logging/retention, KMS integration)
- Minimum platform FTEs and oncall model for pilot (weeks of work + rotation)
- Legal/procurement owner for contracts and any necessary exceptions

I've attached a draft scope (privatenet_scope.xlsx) that splits work into "networking", "runtime", "ops" and "contracting" tabs. I'll schedule a 45m kickoff with Acme + CloudPartner to finalize next week — proposed time in the calendar link below.

Thanks — I want to avoid resourcing ambiguity slowing the pilot.

— Rachel
Rachel Kim
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
rachel_kim@redwood.ai

Attachments: privatenet_scope.xlsx (spreadsheet, 48KB)
From: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.ai>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-03-02T11:05:00Z
Subject: Re: PrivateNet launch criteria & ownership decision

Thanks Rachel — quick architecture runbook notes from my side:

- Topology: For on-prem we should assume a single edge gateway + isolated GPU cluster behind NAT. VPC option is standard private subnet w/ cross-account VPC peering.
- Runtime: We'll need ability to pin quantized variants and a compact KV cache colocated on the local cluster to avoid cross-region egress for hot prompts.
- Minimum HW: proposal = 2x A100 nodes (or 4x T4 if cost constrained) per on-prem site to meet 99th %-tile latency target for the pilot.
- Resourcing: estimate 0.5 FTE Platform Eng (8 weeks) for bootstrap + 0.25 FTE SRE for an initial 2-month oncall window.
- Risks: network egress policies and KMS latency are the biggest unknowns — need a short PoC for KMS round-trip times.

I can own the architecture signoff if Product/Legal are OK with the hardware and oncall asks.

Date: 2028-03-02T14:40:00Z
Subject: Re: PrivateNet launch criteria & ownership decision

Agree with Connor's tech notes — a couple of product clarifications to lock acceptance criteria:

- Functional acceptance: model parity (same prompt/response quality vs hosted), throughput baseline (X gen/s under target latency), and deterministic fallback to hosted if local capacity exhausted.
- Observability: token-level cost and latency must be visible in Console for Acme; telemetry hooks and error traces need to be enabled by default.
- Rollout: start with a strict canary (5% traffic) and manual escalation; we cannot enable automatic fallback without gating tests.

I can be product owner for acceptance criteria + canary decision; Connor to own infra signoff; Lauren to own security gating; Marcus to own contracting. I'll add the acceptance criteria doc here: https://redwood.app/drive/privatenet-launch-criteria

Markus
Product Lead, Core Platform

Date: 2028-03-03T08:22:00Z
Subject: Re: PrivateNet launch criteria & ownership decision

Summary of the security gating items we will require for pilot acceptance (see attached checklist):

- KMS: can connect to customer-managed KMS (preferred) or use our proxy with audit logs.
- Network: TLS mTLS on all internal service traffic; documented firewall rules and egress policies.
- Logging: centralized audit logs forwarded to Acme (90d retention) + token-level sampling for quality monitoring.
- Compliance artifacts: current SOC 2 report, penetration test summary, and data flow diagram.

Attachment: sec_checklist_v2.pdf (PDF, 125KB)

Marissa — can Legal take the lead on the SOC2/contract language? Marcus, please confirm procurement cadence.

— Lauren
Lauren Bishop
Security Engineering Manager
lauren_bishop@redwood.ai

Thanks all — quick decision log and next steps:

- Owners: Architecture = Connor O'Brien; Product acceptance + canary policy = Markus Klein; Security gating = Lauren Bishop; Procurement/contract = Marcus Lin; Legal support = Marissa Cole.
- Resourcing ask acknowledged: Connor to confirm HW BOM and 0.5 FTE Platform commitment by Friday.
- Action: Lauren/Marissa to produce the minimum security deliverables list for procurement (due Tue 2028-03-07).
- Calendar: Kickoff with Acme + CloudPartner scheduled — https://calendar.redwood.ai/meet/privatenet-kickoff-20280304

I'll run the kickoff and capture the mutual action plan. If anyone cannot take the owner role above, call it out now.

— Rachel
